title: Starting to arrange: lead sheets and copied parts
summary: At 'Bama State from 1932 he wrote lead sheets, copied out parts and taught others; everyone in the band could read.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: When did you first begin composing and arranging?
Well, I started to mess around with that as soon as I got to 'Bama State. That was set around '32 I believe because I went there in '31. END T1 P#1

I did a lot of things there. Just things that I just liked to write. I just, like I said, I just made my own cue-sheet. Then, I taught some of the other fellows around there how to make the cue-sheet until he got the right way of going on those cue-sheets.
When you say cue-sheets, you mean a lead sheet?
Okay. And, how did the music get from that lead sheet to the band members? How did you rehearse them?
Well, oh, well, after I copied all the parts out. I had to copy each part and then we'd put it up in rehearsal.
Oh, then you actually made an arrangement then?
You made the whole arrangement and gave them parts.
So, all of the members of the band were reading at that time?
Oh, yes. Everybody was reading. Everybody could read. They had been under some good teachers.
